linesVerbatim: ## Three different meanings of core
V2 uses three terms and does not collapse them:
| Term | Meaning | Boundary |
| **Signed distribution core** | Proposed small native executable plus its mandatory runtime/data closure | Packaging, install, update, trust, management/recovery footprint |

| **Semantic host** | Host authority for admission, Snapshot/Plan, findings/facts, Coverage, policy, finalization, durable authority, D9, and output | May share a process with the distribution core, but authority is non-delegable |

| **Pure evaluation core** | R-1 data-only deterministic evaluation function returning `CoreCompletion` | No effects, callbacks, ports, entropy, filesystem, network, process, store, or resident state |
The distribution core and semantic host may initially be one executable. That
does not permit semantic work to migrate into components or effects into the
pure evaluation core.
## Proposed small signed distribution core
The default install is proposed to contain routing, strict configuration,
authentication, trust, updates, host semantic authority, output, component
protocol/supervision, lifecycle/recovery, and essential lock/journal/audit state.
It excludes language runtimes, analyzers, graph engines, report generators,
evidence databases, and telemetry backends from the default dependency closure.
“Small” is falsifiable, not aesthetic. Every release must publish:
- the complete mandatory file/dependency/TCB inventory and layer assignment;
- exact signed compressed and installed closure size;
- cold help/version startup and baseline/peak memory;
- evidence that help/version/config/status/doctor load no project or component;
- each component's incremental cost; and
- the aggregate authoritative offline closure cost.

threeCores.rule: The three terms are not collapsed.
threeCores.signedDistributionCore: Proposed small native executable plus its mandatory runtime/data closure. Boundary: packaging, install, update, trust, management/recovery footprint.
threeCores.semanticHost: Host authority for admission, Snapshot/Plan, findings/facts, Coverage, policy, finalization, durable authority, D9, and output. Authority is non-delegable. MAY share a process with the distribution core.
threeCores.pureEvaluationCore: R-1 data-only deterministic evaluation function returning CoreCompletion. No effects, callbacks, ports, entropy, filesystem, network, process, store, or resident state.
threeCores.oneExecutableSharing: Distribution core and semantic host may initially be one executable. That does not permit semantic work to migrate into components or effects into the pure evaluation core.

defaultInstall.managementOnly: Core-only is management and recovery: help, version, completion, configuration, component inventory/lifecycle, status, doctor, and repair. It is not the current full analysis product and cannot claim absent capabilities.
defaultInstall.authoritativeOffline: A supported authoritative offline analysis closure is a DIFFERENT signed selection (file 02 L49-58). It is not the default install. Storage backend is DR-106/109 (D-002 deferred wholly). This artifact does not smuggle that backend into the default core.

inventorySchema.dependencyGraph: The published inventory is a directed requires-graph of digest-pinned file nodes. Required members are defined here. Layer-set cardinality, lawful overlap, and the shared-executable representation are defined at inventorySchema.graphRules. Which layer a non-shared node takes follows layerTaxonomy. The L-TCB boundary is DR-126's per ID-DEP-K2. Undeclared nodes are a failed successor (qualitative half joins DR-126). This artifact does not populate the per-OS table.
inventorySchema.signingRolesNote: Role list is inventory/identity (file 03 proposed independent-release trust). Ceremony, thresholds, and OS notarization remain OD-101-2 on this row. DR-112 / DR-110 supply adjacent ceremony/repair-media mechanics; they do not own this fragment.

graphRules.nodeGranularity: One graph node per digest-pinned published file path (NFC, relative, forward-slash). Directories are not nodes. The shared distribution+host executable is exactly one node.
graphRules.nodeIdentity: {path, sha256}. Duplicate path is a failed successor. Duplicate sha256 under a different path is a failed successor. This version defines no alias edge relation. Aliases are reserved and unavailable to successors of this version until a later owner defines a closed alias relation (direction, endpoints, eligibility, layer assignment, root/cycle/closure treatment, and filesystem-alias vs independent equal-content files). Until then both a filesystem alias and two independent equal-content files fail.
graphRules.roots: Exactly the nodes that no other node requires. The default-install closure MUST include at least one root. The shared executable, if present, is a root unless another published file requires it.
graphRules.edgeRelation: Directed 'requires' from consumer to dependency. No undirected edges. Cycles are a failed successor.
graphRules.layerAssignmentCardinality: Each node has a non-empty set of layers. Exclusive layers: L-EVAL and L-COMP MUST NOT co-occur with any other layer. Lawful overlap: only {L-DIST, L-HOST} on the single shared executable node. L-TCB nodes are exclusive L-TCB.
graphRules.sharedExecutableRepresentation: When threeCores.oneExecutableSharing applies, emit one node whose layer set is {L-DIST, L-HOST}. Do not emit two nodes with the same sha256. Do not emit L-DIST-only or L-HOST-only for that file. Authority non-migration is unchanged: sharing the node does not move semantic-host authority into a component or effects into L-EVAL.
graphRules.doesNotPopulate: These rules fix layer-set cardinality, lawful overlap, and the shared-executable representation. They do not decide which exclusive layer a non-shared node takes (layerTaxonomy; L-TCB is DR-126). They do not populate the per-OS table.
graphRules.lEvalPublication: L-EVAL is a layer tag on inventory nodes. This artifact does not require L-EVAL bytes to be a separately published file, and does not forbid it. Whether any L-EVAL node is a distinct published artifact versus in-process is reserved to the publisher of those bytes and is not decided here.
